instructions: Correct only the erroneous Antigravity permission-flag expectation in the parameterized native-policy propagation and early-completion test for PRIMARY, REMEDIATION and REPAIR. When mutation is authorized, its already-existing command includes --dangerously-skip-permissions; when mutation is not authorized, the flag is absent.

Keep the Antigravity adapter and its pre-existing permission behavior unchanged. Preserve the existing --mode accept-edits expectation for mutation-authorized calls and verify that read-only invocations do not acquire mutation flags.

Retain all TASK-357 AC1-AC5 implementation and prior regression coverage, including provider-neutral 180-minute response and 185-minute watchdog policy, original diagnostics and unknown exit treatment, and early completion without retry. Make no changes beyond the minimum in-scope test correction necessary to remove the false expectation.

Provide a clean committed correction candidate with truthful structural claims; allow Runtime alone to execute the exact already-authored minimum-sufficient-v1 verification command and determine canonical evidence. No full-suite run, bypass, fabricated PASS or self-publication.

acceptance.condition: The existing provider-neutral native execution policy has a 180-minute response budget and a finite 185-minute process watchdog, with no alternative default or task-specific override.

PRIMARY, REMEDIATION and REPAIR invocation construction exposes the same policy values through Codex, Antigravity and Antigravity-Minimax adapters without changing their permitted authority or model selection.
Native timeout handling still terminates one admitted invocation with a truthful timeout and original captured diagnostics; absent native exit status is represented as unknown rather than fabricated.
Native responses received before the deadline return normally without artificial waiting, automatic retry, executor substitution or follow-on dispatch.
Deterministic synthetic regression coverage exists for the exact budget, watchdog, provider/operation propagation, normal early completion and timeout/error behaviors of the existing native paths.

assumptions: This is a new independent TASK revision 1 against the canonical published main current at AUTHOR_TASK admission; Runtime rechecks expected-main currentness, schema, scope, provenance and CAS. Unreviewed worktrees or earlier failed RUN candidates are not input sources or execution bases.
Human owns acceptance of the longer possible stall exposure and chooses the Executor separately. This TASK does not select a model or create a RUN.

Existing NativeExecutionPolicy and Codex, Antigravity and Antigravity-Minimax adapters remain the single native execution mechanism. No execution can use the newly authored default as published policy until exact reviewed publication.

hard: Use the existing provider-neutral NativeExecutionPolicy rather than a second deadline source. Preserve the response budget versus process-watchdog distinction.

Keep precisely one admitted Executor call; early successful returns complete immediately, timeout remains terminal, and unknown native exit codes remain unknown instead of fabricated success or failure.
Do not change Runtime verification requirements, review/publication boundaries, native lease ownership, sandbox policy, source mutation rights or failure provenance.
Use deterministic synthetic native runners to test deadlines and timeout propagation. Do not sleep 180 minutes or repeat unchanged whole-suite tests.

task.goal: Prospectively increase the existing provider-neutral native coding Executor response budget to 180 minutes and the bounded process watchdog to 185 minutes, consistently across admitted PRIMARY, REMEDIATION and REPAIR paths without changing Runtime verification or correction authority.
non_goals: No public FAILURE diagnostic projection, Brain Sync, transport or private-evidence redesign.
No new Kernel semantics, planner, controller, watchdog service, retry/failover selector or mutation authority.
No per-TASK or per-provider deadline exceptions, ambient overrides or unbounded waiting.
No rewriting historical RUN, FAILURE, RESULT, EVIDENCE, REVIEW or publication states.
task.problem: The published native execution policy currently permits 60 minutes of model response and a 65-minute process watchdog. Legitimate long-running engineering invocations can exceed that budget before producing a structural ResultPackage. The desired bounded default should be consistently applied through existing native adapters rather than per-TASK overrides, new services or automatic retries.
